# Roadmap

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_roadmap.py from docs/DESIGN.md section 6; do not edit. -->

Where Cuervo Engine is going, phase by phase. Each milestone has a goal it is "done"
when; the design behind each one is in [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) (the section after its
title), and what works today is in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md). Changing the roadmap is a
design change, described in CONTRIBUTING.md ("Design Changes").

37 of 55 milestones are done.

## Phase 0: Skeleton

CMake, SDL3 window, fixed-timestep loop, input actions, logging, `Vec<T,N>`, RHI interface + GL and Vulkan backends (Vulkan pulled forward from Phase 5)

**Partly done.** Done when: A window clears to a color and responds to actions, on Linux and Windows

## Phase 1: Language core

(in parallel): lexer, parser, type checker, bytecode, VM, refcounting, REPL

**Done.** Done when: Closures, structs, classes and enums run in the REPL; language test suite passes

## Phase 2: Vector rendering

SDF batcher, SVG import + tessellation, MSDF text, camera, scale modes

**Done.** Done when: 50k SDF shapes at 60 fps; an SVG character drawn sharp at any zoom

## Phase 3: Integration

bindings, scripts on nodes, coroutines, hot reload

**Done.** Done when: **A shmup stage written entirely in the language**

## Phase 4: Gameplay systems

particle system (gameplay + visual), collision, audio, UI nodes, binary scenes + dump

**Done.** Done when: A playable boss fight with menus

## Phase 5: Web + tiers

WebGL2 export, Vulkan feature parity, tiers + migration report

**Planned.** Done when: The same project runs on Linux, Windows and the web (Linux + web done and verified, docs/WEB.md; Windows validation is in progress on Intel Arc integrated graphics and an RTX 4070 on the Core Ultra 9 185H laptop: the Clang debug build passes `ctest` and reaches the Linux hashes, docs/WINDOWS.md)

- **5.5 Performance core (§4.15)** (done). activate the job system, explicit SIMD (AVX2 / WASM SIMD128), sub-seeded RNG streams, secondary spatial hash for large shapes
  Done when: The particle demo's sim time scales with worker count, SIMD and scalar paths are bit-identical, and the replay hash is unchanged at 1 and N threads

## Phase 6: Editor

scene view, inspector, assets, play-in-editor, replay viewer

**Done.** Done when: A level can be built without code

## Phase 7: Release path

AOT-to-C, cycle collector, manual memory, packing, export

**Done.** Done when: A shipped build runs measurably faster than the VM

- **7.5 Modular footprint** (done). Feature-stripping build system, dead-code elimination, unreferenced module pruning
  Done when: An exported project strips unused engine subsystems (e.g., audio, unused RHI features, UI) resulting in measurably smaller release binaries and web payloads

## Phase 8: Tooling

formatter, LSP, debugger, animation (cutout, skeletal, morph), docs (expanded as 8.4)

**Planned.** Done when: Someone else makes a game with it (tooling done, animation deferred to 9.4: formatter and LSP, debugger over DAP, and profiler, §5.14 "Clarified (Phase 8 — ...)"; the VS Code extension `tools/vscode-pluma`; docs/GUIDE.md with the `examples/tutorial` game and the generated docs/API.md, expanded further by 8.4. All of 8.1-8.9 are done; the done-when needs an outside user to confirm)

- **8.1 Brand integration (§4.16)** (done). Cuervo Mark, wordmark, palette and type from the design kit, synced into `assets/brand/`, plus generated color tokens
  Done when: The editor and runtime show the mark as window icon and splash in light and dark themes, and a sync script regenerates the brand assets from the kit

- **8.2 Node library (§4.16)** (done). Shape, Path, Sprite, Text, Camera2D, Timer, Area, Emitter2D, AudioPlayer as prelude nodes
  Done when: A level using every new node is built in the editor without code and round-trips through scene files with the same state hash

- **8.3 Editor UI overhaul (§4.16)** (done). themed with the brand tokens, gizmos, toolbar, command palette, multi-select, undo history, welcome screen
  Done when: The `examples/editor_level` workflow is redone with gizmos and the palette, with no raw ImGui-default styling left

- **8.4 Documentation (§4.16)** (done). manual, Pluma guide, generated API/node reference, first-game tutorial, branded static site
  Done when: Every public prelude symbol is documented (enforced by a test) and the tutorial game builds in CI

- **8.5 Documentation reconciliation (§4.16)** (done). align design, user and API documentation with the actual MIT license, current milestone state, implemented systems, and support status; separate shipped, experimental, planned and unsupported behavior
  Done when: A fresh reader can determine what is implemented and supported without relying on historical milestone notes; no active document claims that the license is undecided or that completed systems are still only planned

- **8.6 Performance baselines (§4.15)** (done). publish repeatable simulation, render, memory and export-size measurements for representative particle/shape loads, native backends, WebGL2, debug and release builds
  Done when: Benchmark commands record versioned baselines and flag regressions when agreed thresholds are exceeded; the 1k/10k/50k/100k workload results are reproducible on the reference machine

- **8.7 Stabilization pass (§4.12, §4.13, §5)** (done). prioritize Pluma semantics, scene serialization and migrations, editor workflows, replay behavior and export reliability before another major subsystem
  Done when: A clean checkout can build the reference examples, round-trip scenes, hot-reload scripts, verify replays and launch source, AOT and stripped exports without known correctness regressions

- **8.8 Supported-features contract (§4.4, §4.16)** (done). classify features as stable, experimental, desktop-only, Web-compatible or unsupported; document the guarantees and limits of `compatible` and `full` render tiers
  Done when: The README and generated/user documentation expose the same support matrix, and tier checks reject configurations that claim support the selected target does not provide

- **8.9 End-to-end user workflow (§4.11, §4.13)** (done). automate the fresh-checkout path from project creation through scene editing, running, exporting and launching the exported game
  Done when: A workflow smoke test creates or opens a project, edits and saves a scene, runs it, exports it, launches the shipped artifact outside the project directory and verifies its exit status and deterministic state hash

## Phase 9: Advanced Local Systems (§4.17)

transform hierarchy and more nodes, Pluma library, UI widgets, animation, tilemaps and navigation, Box2D v3 physics, 2D SDF lighting/raymarching

**Done.** Done when: A physics-based platformer with 2D lighting is playable

- **9.1 Transform hierarchy and node gaps (§4.17)** (done). parent-relative transforms (toggleable), `Line2D`, `Polygon2D`, `Marker2D`, `VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D`
  Done when: Moving a parent moves its children when the hierarchy is on, and world-space scenes behave exactly as before with it off

- **9.2a Pluma collections, strings and language (§4.17)** (done). `Map`/`Set`/fixed arrays/`StrBuilder`, `List` and `str` methods, conversions, property accessors, `Result` and `?`, method values
  Done when: A script uses each feature and the language test suite passes under the VM and AOT

- **9.2b Pluma math, geometry and random (§4.17)** (done). scalar/integer/vector math, `Rect2`, `Transform2D`, geometry helpers, noise, seeded `Random` streams
  Done when: Every function is bit-identical across SIMD, scalar, VM and AOT, and the replay hash is unchanged

- **9.3 UI widgets (§4.17)** (done). `GridContainer`, `ScrollContainer`, Flow/Split/AspectRatio, `Image`/`TextureRect`, `ProgressBar`, `LineEdit`, `OptionButton`, tabs, popups
  Done when: A settings and inventory menu built from them is driven by keyboard, gamepad and pointer, and replays

- **9.4 Animation (§4.17)** (done). `AnimationPlayer` (property tracks), `Tween`, `AnimationTree` state machine
  Done when: An animated character blends between states and the replay hash is unchanged at 1 and N threads

- **9.5 Tilemaps and navigation (§4.17)** (done). `TileMapLayer`, tilesets, autotiling, `NavigationRegion2D`, `NavigationAgent2D`
  Done when: A top-down level is painted in the editor and an agent paths around obstacles

- **9.6 Physics (§4.17)** (done). Box2D v3 behind the physics interface; `StaticBody2D`, `CharacterBody2D`, `RigidBody2D`, `Area2D`, `CollisionShape2D`, raycasts, joints
  Done when: A platformer character runs, jumps and pushes bodies deterministically

- **9.7 2D lighting (§4.17)** (done). SDF lighting/raymarching, `PointLight2D`, occluders
  Done when: Lights and shadows render identically on Vulkan and GL

- **9.8 Integration (§4.17)** (done). editor support for all of the above and a sample game
  Done when: A physics-based platformer with 2D lighting is playable

## Phase 10: Next-Gen Web

WebGPU, WASM multithreading (SharedArrayBuffer)

**Done.** Done when: A stable benchtest runs natively in the browser (WASM threads done early: docs/WEB.md "Threads", `CUERVO_WEB_THREADS`. **Design decision:** the WebGPU backend's shaders are translated SPIR-V → WGSL by **naga** (Rust; a host build tool), keeping one GLSL 450 source per shader; WebGPU starts only after Phases 8 and 9 are done)

- **10.1 WebGPU backend skeleton (§4.4)** (done). naga pinned as a host tool, `cuervo_add_shaders` also emits WGSL from the same SPIR-V, an `rhi` WebGPU device that clears, draws a triangle and presents on native and in the browser
  Done when: The clear and triangle scenes of `rhi_parity` render through WebGPU and match GL; the native WebGPU implementation used for testing is chosen here and recorded in §4.4

- **10.2 WebGPU feature parity (§4.4–4.6)** (done). every RHI feature in the `cuervo/rhi/README.md` audit table (buffers, textures, pipelines, stream buffers, frame limit, particle compute, SDF lighting) on WebGPU
  Done when: `rhi_parity` compares every scene on WebGPU against GL within the Vulkan tolerance, and the WGSL for every engine shader is generated with no hand-written WGSL

- **10.3 WebGPU web runtime and export (§4.11)** (done). the web build uses WebGPU when the browser has it and falls back to WebGL2 otherwise; `export --platform web` ships both; works with `CUERVO_WEB_THREADS`
  Done when: `examples/shmup` and `examples/lantern_cave` run in headless Chrome on WebGPU and on the WebGL2 fallback, reaching their dev state hashes

- **10.4 Browser benchtest (§4.6)** (done). `examples/bench` in the browser on WebGPU with threads, `tools/bench.py` browser runs and recorded web baselines in docs/perf
  Done when: The browser benchtest runs stably on WebGPU (no frame-time cliffs over its run, regression compare passing), which closes milestone 10

- **10.5 Windows and language APIs (§4.18)** (done). Windows builds, module/package system, plugin and embedding API, FFI
  Done when: The shmup builds, passes its tests and exports on Windows with the same state hash as Linux, and a third-party plugin and package are used by a game

- **10.5a Windows builds (§4.18)** (done). MSVC and MinGW builds, CI, determinism check, signed prebuilt editor and export templates
  Done when: `ctest` passes on Windows and a Windows export of `examples/shmup` reaches the Linux state hash

- **10.5b Modules, packages and unit tests (§4.18)** (done). `import`, namespaces, project dependencies, versioning, plus native `@test` runner in Pluma
  Done when: A game imports a package from another directory with no global name clashes, and `cuervo-tools test` / `plm test` runs pure-logic `@test` functions with pass/fail reporting in CI

- **10.5c Plugin, embedding and FFI APIs (§4.18)** (done). stable C ABI for native modules, C++, Rust and C# bindings, Pluma FFI to C libraries, API versioning
  Done when: A native plugin written in each of C++, Rust and C# adds a node and a function that a script uses (C# on desktop), in the VM and in AOT where supported

- **10.5d Plugin ecosystem, licenses and contribution (§4.18)** (done). plugin manifest and registry, project license, third-party notices, contribution guides
  Done when: The repo has a license, generated third-party notices and contribution docs, and a plugin published to the registry installs into a fresh project and passes the checks

## Phase 11: Production features (§4.19)

rollback/lockstep networking, raster processes and sprite pipeline, custom shaders and post-processing, localization and text shaping, profiler and save/settings API

**Planned.** Done when: A networked two-player game with a localized UI, a custom post-process shader and an atlas-based sprite scene is shipped and profiled

- **11.1 Networking (§4.19)** (planned). transport, lockstep and rollback on the deterministic sim, HTTP and WebSocket
  Done when: Two clients on different machines (native and web) stay in sync, with the same state hash every tick

- **11.2a Raster processes (§4.19)** (planned). image import, texture atlasing, sprite sheet slicing, SVG rasterized fallback, textured quad batcher, `Sprite2D`/`AnimatedSprite2D`, 9-slice, filtering modes
  Done when: An atlas-batched sprite scene with 9-slice panels and rasterized SVG fallbacks renders identically on Vulkan, GL and WebGL2

- **11.2b Shaders, post-processing and linear color (§4.19)** (planned). user shaders (GLSL 450), parameter binding in inspector, off-screen render targets, multi-pass post-processing (bloom, blur, blits), optional linear color space
  Done when: A custom user shader and a multi-pass post-process effect render identically on Vulkan and GL; `project.toml` supports `color_space = "srgb"` or `"linear"`

- **11.2c Text scenes on save (§4.19)** (planned). human-readable text format becomes the default save format in `scenes/`; automatic compile to binary `.pak` on export
  Done when: Saving in the editor writes human-readable scene text that Git can 3-way auto-merge without binary merge conflicts; release exports pack them into binary `.scene` files with zero runtime overhead

- **11.3 Localization and text (§4.19)** (planned). translation tables, complex-script shaping, bidirectional text, IME
  Done when: A UI switches between English, Arabic and Japanese at run time and `LineEdit` accepts IME input

- **11.4 Profiling and save API (§4.19)** (planned). frame/job/GPU profiler, memory profiler, general save/load and settings API
  Done when: A profile of the shmup shows per-system tick cost, and a game saves and restores progress and settings

## Phase 12: Content tools, AI and accessibility (§4.20)

dialogue and cutscene tools, particle and shader editors, behavior trees and steering, accessibility, the ECS resolution

**Planned.** Done when: A narrative game with AI enemies and a screen-reader-usable menu is built mostly in the editor

- **12.1 Content tools (§4.20)** (planned). visual node-graph canvas (`imgui-node-editor`), dialogue and cutscene/timeline editor, particle editor UI, visual shader editor
  Done when: A cutscene with dialogue and a particle effect is authored without code using visual graph panels

- **12.2 AI (§4.20)** (planned). behavior trees, state-machine tool, steering behaviors
  Done when: An enemy with a behavior tree is built and debugged in the editor

- **12.3 Accessibility and editor polish (§4.20)** (planned). AccessKit integration (screen-reader support), UI scaling, remapping, desktop file drag-and-drop, crisp DPI font oversampling
  Done when: The shmup menus can be used with a screen reader and at 200% UI scale; platform screen readers read UI elements via AccessKit; desktop file drag-and-drop into viewport functions

- **12.4 The ECS resolution (§4.20)** (planned). finalize the Hybrid Architecture (Godot-style `Node2D` hierarchy for scene logic + contiguous internal SoA pools exposed via Pluma query loops)
  Done when: The decision is documented: scripts iterate bulk entities via deterministic queries (`for e in query(Enemy)`) in the job system without exposing raw low-level ECS internals

## Phase 13: Extended Platforms & drop-in console SDKs (§4.21)

macOS (MoltenVK), iOS, Android (SDL3 + GLES 3.0), mobile lifecycle/thermal mitigation, drop-in Console C ABI

**Planned.** Done when: The shmup runs natively on a Mac, iPhone, and Android device; developers with private console DevKits drop closed-source C ABI shims in without engine forks

## Phase 14: Zero-bloat 3D Expansion (§4.22)

3D rendering pipeline, 3D math (`Vec<T,N>`), 3D scene/camera transforms, glTF import, PBR materials

**Planned.** Done when: A full 3D scene runs with PBR materials and 3D transforms; 2D exports strip all 3D pipelines via Milestone 7.5 dead-code elimination with 0 bytes overhead

## Phase 15: First-party jumpstart ecosystem (§4.23)

official C ABI plugin wrappers (`cuervo-steamworks`, `cuervo-spine`, `cuervo-fmod`, `cuervo-console-template`) and genre showcase demos

**Planned.** Done when: Shipped templates for a 2-player rollback brawler, a 100k-particle survivors game, and turn-key Steamworks/Spine/FMOD wrappers unblock commercial shipping
